sample_unit: synthetic discharge summaries and patient record retrieval queries

links.outcome: Embedding model detection of direction of semantic change under controlled text perturbations
links.effect: On average models detected direction of change correctly, but case-level performance varied; Qwen3-Embedding-8B had zero directional errors while multilingual-E5-large erred in 13.8% of cases.
links.quote: Qwen3-Embedding-8B was the only model with zero directional errors, while multilingual-E5-large erred in 13.8% of cases.

links.outcome: Performance differences between candidate embedding models on the same clinical tasks
links.effect: Qwen3-Embedding-8B outperformed multilingual-E5-large in retrieval; sufficiency 3.25 vs 3.17 for first query and 2.25 vs 1.15 out of 5 for second query.
links.quote: Our results show that the choice of embedding model is important: performance differences between models can be large enough to determine whether clinically relevant information reaches the end user, and model weaknesses can be both task-specific and context-dependent.

screen.reason: Evaluates embedding models for clinical text semantic difference detection and RAG-style data retrieval from records, comparing performance across various models and distance metrics without evaluating a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
